def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp:
## Definition

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $H\in C^\infty(D,(0,\infty))$ be independent of time. Write $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ for length coordinates, set $x^0=ct$ when a time variable is used, and require $H$ to be dimensionless. The ordinary Euclidean Laplacian is $\Delta_\delta H:=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i^2H$; call $H$ harmonic when $\Delta_\delta H=0$. Take $\mathcal M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$, with orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ and future direction selected by $N_H=H\partial_{x^0}$.

For a sign $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$ define the metric and global potential one-form

$$g_H=-H^{-2}(dx^0)^2+H^2\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2,\qquad \mathcal A_\sigma=\sigma(H^{-1}-1)\,dx^0.$$

The associated two-form is

$$\mathcal F_\sigma:=d\mathcal A_\sigma=-\sigma\sum_{i=1}^3\frac{H_i}{H^2}\,dx^i\wedge dx^0,\qquad H_i:=\partial_iH.$$

The **positive harmonic conformastatic electrovac data** are the tuple $(\mathcal M,g_H,N_H,o,\mathcal F_\sigma)$ for these choices. The metric is the chart tensor of [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]] and is Lorentzian with the stated future direction by [[lem-emg-conformastatic-chart-is-lorentzian]]. The term “electrovac data” names a candidate for the equations in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]; this definition by itself does not assert that the equations hold. The field components have inverse-length units in length coordinates, so the Ricci and quadratic-field components both have inverse-length-squared units.
def-emg-xs-br-products:
## Definition

Let $S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:|n|=1\}$ carry its induced unit round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$ and outward area form $\omega_{S^2}$. Let $L>0$ have length units. Choose either (i) $f(z)=z^2$ on an open $J\subset(0,\infty)$, or (ii) $f(z)=1+z^2$ on an open $J\subset\mathbb R$. The coordinate $z$ and $\tau$ are dimensionless. On $\mathcal M_{L,f}=\mathbb R_\tau\times J_z\times S^2$, orient by $d\tau\wedge dz\wedge\omega_{S^2}$ and define

$$g_{L,f}=L^2\bigl(-f(z)d\tau^2+f(z)^{-1}dz^2+\gamma_{S^2}\bigr),\qquad \mathcal F_L=-L\,d\tau\wedge dz.$$

The smooth field $N=(L\sqrt{f})^{-1}\partial_\tau$ is unit timelike; it selects the future direction. This explicit metric-field tuple is the **Bertotti-Robinson product data** for this library. “Electrovac” refers to the equations in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] and is not asserted by this definition. The product has sphere radius $L$ at every base point.
def-emg-xs-null-wave:
## Definition

Use length coordinates $(u,v,x,y)$ on $\mathbb R^4$. Let $a,b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth profiles with inverse-length units, and let $h:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth dimensionless function satisfying $h_{xx}+h_{yy}=0$ at every $(u,x,y)$. Define the dimensionless function

$$P(u,x,y)=-(a(u)^2+b(u)^2)(x^2+y^2)+h(u,x,y).$$

With orientation $du\wedge dv\wedge dx\wedge dy$, define

$$g=-2\,du\,dv+dx^2+dy^2+P\,du^2,\qquad \mathcal A=-(a(u)x+b(u)y)\,du,\qquad \mathcal F=d\mathcal A=a(u)\,du\wedge dx+b(u)\,du\wedge dy.$$

The vector field $N=\partial_u+\frac{P+1}{2}\partial_v$ has $g(N,N)=-1$ and selects the future direction. The $u,v$ block of $g$ has determinant $-1$, so together with the two positive transverse directions this is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $\sqrt{|\det g|}=1$. The tuple $(\mathbb R^4,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ is the **null-wave candidate data** for the equations of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]; no field-equation claim is part of this definition. The metric coefficients are dimensionless, and $\mathcal F_{ui}$ has inverse-length units.
thm-emg-xs-mp-verification:
## Statement

Every datum of [[def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp]] satisfies the source-free geometric Einstein-Maxwell equations of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]:

$$d\mathcal F_\sigma=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F_\sigma)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F_\sigma),\quad Q_{ab}(F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}.$$

More explicitly, with $q_H:=\sum_iH_i^2$, the only nonzero independent raised field components are $\mathcal F^{i0}_\sigma=\sigma H_i/H^2$ and the quadratic-field components are

$$\mathcal F_{\sigma,ab}\mathcal F_\sigma^{ab}=-\frac{2q_H}{H^4},\qquad Q_{00}=\frac{q_H}{2H^6},\qquad Q_{0i}=0,\qquad Q_{ij}=\frac{\delta_{ij}q_H-2H_iH_j}{2H^2}.$$
thm-emg-xs-br-verification:
## Statement

Every datum in [[def-emg-xs-br-products]] is a geometric electrovac datum of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. With the oriented orthonormal coframe

$$e^0=L\sqrt f\,d\tau,\quad e^1=L f^{-1/2}dz,\quad e^2=L\,d\theta,\quad e^3=L\sin\theta\,d\phi,$$

the Ricci and quadratic Maxwell tensors are

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{AB}=L^{-2}\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,1)_{AB},\qquad Q_{AB}(\mathcal F_L)=\frac1{2L^2}\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,1)_{AB}.$$

All mixed base-sphere entries vanish. The statement is on the chosen open chart domains; it makes no maximal-extension or asymptotic-flatness claim.
thm-emg-xs-null-wave-verification:
## Statement

Every candidate datum in [[def-emg-xs-null-wave]] is a smooth source-free geometric electrovac datum in the convention of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. Its only nonzero Ricci component is

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{uu}=2(a(u)^2+b(u)^2),$$

and its Maxwell quadratic tensor has only $Q_{uu}=a(u)^2+b(u)^2$ nonzero. Thus $\operatorname{Ric}=2Q(\mathcal F)$ for arbitrary smooth profiles $a,b$ and every smooth transverse harmonic addition $h$ specified in the definition. No asymptotic-flatness or finite-energy assertion is included.
prop-emg-xs-mp-multicenter:
## Statement

Let $N\ge1$ be an integer, let $a_1,\ldots,a_N\in\mathbb R^3$ be distinct, let $m_A>0$ have length units, and let $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$. On $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{a_1,\ldots,a_N\}$ define

$$H(x)=1+\sum_{A=1}^N\frac{m_A}{|x-a_A|}.$$

Then $H$ is smooth, positive and Euclidean harmonic on $D$, so [[def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp]] and [[thm-emg-xs-mp-verification]] give a smooth source-free geometric electrovac datum on $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$. For each $A$, every coordinate sphere $S_A(r)=\{x:|x-a_A|=r\}$ whose closed ball contains no other center has electric flux $q_e(S_A(r))=\sigma m_A$ and magnetic flux $q_m(S_A(r))=0$. If a coordinate sphere $S_R=\{x:|x|=R\}$ strictly encloses all centers, its fluxes are $q_e(S_R)=\sigma\sum_A m_A$ and $q_m(S_R)=0$. No center is included in the manifold; these are fluxes through regular spheres, not matter-source, horizon-extension, stability, or completeness claims.
prop-emg-xs-null-invariants:
## Statement

For every null-wave electrovac datum of [[def-emg-xs-null-wave]] and [[thm-emg-xs-null-wave-verification]],

$$\mathcal F_{ab}\mathcal F^{ab}=0,\qquad S=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\operatorname{Ric}^{ab}=0,\qquad R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=0.$$

In the displayed coordinates the only potentially nonzero independent Riemann components are

$$R_{uiuj}=-\frac12P_{ij},\qquad i,j\in\{x,y\}.$$

If $a(u_0)^2+b(u_0)^2>0$ at any $u_0$, then the Riemann tensor is nonzero there; the metric is not flat. Here $R_{abcd}$ and $S$ use the convention in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]].
prop-emg-xs-mp-extremal-rn:
## Statement

Let $m>0$ have length units, let $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$, put $\rho=|x|$ on $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, and use $H=1+m/\rho$ in [[def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp]]. Under the radial diffeomorphism $R=\rho+m$ from $\rho>0$ to $R>m$, the full metric and field data equal the dyonic Reissner-Nordström datum of [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]] with

$$M=m,\qquad q_e=\sigma m,\qquad q_m=0,\qquad f(R)=\left(1-\frac mR\right)^2.$$

The parameters satisfy $|q_e|=M$; this is the extremal parameter relation in the displayed RN convention. By [[thm-emg-xs-mp-verification]] and the geometric clause of [[thm-emg-xs-rn-verification]], these identical exterior data satisfy the source-free geometric electrovac equations. The identification is only between the open exteriors $\rho>0$ and $R>m$; no horizon extension or global completeness follows.
thm-emg-xs-rn-near-horizon:
## Statement

Fix $L>0$ and take the extremal RN datum with $M=q_e=L$, $q_m=0$, on $r>L$ in [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]]. For each dimensionless $\lambda>0$, define

$$\Phi_\lambda(T,R,\omega)=(x^0=T/\lambda,\ r=L+\lambda R,\ \omega),\qquad (T,R,\omega)\in\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times S^2.$$

Writing $g_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda^*g$ and $\mathcal F_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda^*\mathcal F$, one has

$$g_\lambda=-\frac{R^2}{(L+\lambda R)^2}\,dT^2+\frac{(L+\lambda R)^2}{R^2}\,dR^2+(L+\lambda R)^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad \mathcal F_\lambda=-\frac{L}{(L+\lambda R)^2}\,dT\wedge dR.$$

As $\lambda\downarrow0$, these tensors converge in $C^\infty_{\rm loc}$ on $\mathbb R_T\times(0,\infty)_R\times S^2$ to

$$g_0=-\frac{R^2}{L^2}dT^2+\frac{L^2}{R^2}dR^2+L^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad \mathcal F_0=-\frac1L\,dT\wedge dR.$$

Under $T=L\tau$, $R=Lz$, the limiting datum is exactly the $f(z)=z^2$, $z>0$ product in [[def-emg-xs-br-products]], and it is a geometric electrovac datum by [[thm-emg-xs-br-verification]]. Here $C^\infty_{\rm loc}$ means uniform convergence of every coordinate derivative on every compact subset in a finite smooth atlas. The convergence is only on $R>0$; no extension or convergence across $R=0$ is asserted.
